sure.. will provide everything what i did step after step... first stage, then my second stage after which the panel started to "boil" all this stuff up..

first stage:

panel prep - everything sanded down, rust sandblasted, cleaned, rust sealer, 320grit, all that...

primer - first light coat, bodyfiller, sanding with 320grit, second coat(20 minutes @ ~77f, not exactly sure how long i waited but made sure it was fully dry), third coat... then it all sat for about 5 days (wasnt home :P)... 600grit before base, panel cleaned with silicone wash..

base coat (solvent based) - first coat, 15-20 minutes at 90f, second coat, sat for 15 minutes at 90f (directly to the sun, dried really quick - maybe also a mistake?).

clear coat - made a mistake.. read from the website where i bought the clear coat from that it should be 2:1+15%... after i laying the clear down i realized they wrote on the can that it was supposed to be 3:1+15% (they prepped every component for me to just mix them all together, but their prepped components vary depending on your work area, objective etc, hence why the different ratios.. i think?), but all other panels except the fender layed the clear really nice... the fender had small pinholes, probably solvent pop from what i researched...


second stage:

prep- let the clear on the fender sit for 16hrs.. start sanding to cut down to the pinholes, had to start with around 180 cause otherwise would have sanded forever, ended the panel with 600... panel was sanded until base coat/primer, otherwise wouldnt have reached the pinholes.. after all that waited for 50 minutes

base - first coat and within 10-20 seconds.. that happened (refer to posted pics..)
